newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish insurer Codan plans cost reductions.
newsitem.headline: Danish insurer Codan plans cost reductions.

text.p: Danish insurance group Codan plans to reduce costs to an amount equal to 25 percent of premium revenues, from their present 29 percent, over the next two years, Managing Director Peter Zobel said on Wednesday.
He said that staff levels needed to be cut from the present roster of 2,730 -- where salary bills account for 70 percent of overall costs -- but he planned no major redundancies.
"There should be fewer employees but we are not going in for big firing rounds. It can happen through natural wastage," he said in an interview.
He would not say by how much he intended to cut numbers.
"One of management's most essential tasks is to run the business with as few employees as possible," he said.
Codan, 71.45 percent owned by Britain's Royal and Sun Alliance, is Denmark's second-biggest accident insurer.
It reported 1996 first-half pre-tax profits of 443 million crowns compared to 178 million in the first six months of 1995 and said it expected growth to continue in the second half.
